prompt.context: Syzygy Supercomputers is a large international fully-integrated computers and communications company with annual revenues of approximately $20 billion U.S. In the past several years, the company has seen a steady decline in profits.
prompt.question: The CEO has asked us to look into this problem. How can Syzygy Supercomputers get back on track?

clarifying_info.q: What is driving the revenue decline — is it pricing or volume?
clarifying_info.a: No specific information on that is currently available beyond what has been provided.

clarifying_info.q: How does the competitive landscape look — are competitors gaining share?
clarifying_info.a: There are several players in the market, but everything has remained stable from a competitive standpoint.

clarifying_info.q: Are COGS or SG&A out of line with industry norms?
clarifying_info.a: COGS, SG&A, and other profitability factors are on-par with Syzygy's competitors (except for R&D, about which the candidate should ask specifically).

exhibits.title: Syzygy's Historical Costs, Revenues and Profits
exhibits.shows: A multi-year time series chart showing Syzygy's total revenues, total costs, and profits over time, illustrating the trend of declining profitability
exhibits.data: Annual revenues ~$20B; profits declining over multiple years; cost lines visible by category

exhibits.title: Worldwide Telecom Computing Market (Today)
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar or bubble chart showing multiple product categories (custom applications, supercomputers, telecom equipment, satellites, operating software) with Syzygy's market share vs. competitors for each category
exhibits.data: Product categories represented as rectangles; height indicates market share; competitor rectangles shown alongside Syzygy's for each product

exhibits.title: Syzygy's Absolute vs. Relative Market Share
exhibits.shows: A bubble chart with Absolute Market Share (AMS) on the X-axis and Relative Market Share (RMS) on the Y-axis; bubble diameter driven by Syzygy's total revenues in each category; five numbered bubbles representing the five product categories
exhibits.data: X-axis: Absolute Market Share; Y-axis: Relative Market Share (Syzygy share / closest competitor share); RMS>1 means Syzygy is market leader; five bubbles labeled #1 through #5

exhibits.title: Companies' R&D vs. Degree of Technical Leadership
exhibits.shows: A scatter plot of multiple competitors (including Syzygy, Cray Research, Sonic Wave, and others) plotting R&D spending against perceived degree of technical leadership from customers, with a normative band indicated
exhibits.data: Syzygy data point visible; normative band shown; Syzygy is the only major competitor below the normative band; Cray Research and Sonic Wave shown with slightly less R&D spending

exhibits.title: Syzygy's R&D Expenses and Selling Prices for Supercomputers
exhibits.shows: A chart showing the breakdown of Syzygy's R&D expenditures by feature type alongside the corresponding selling prices or customer willingness-to-pay for supercomputers
exhibits.data: R&D expense amounts by feature; selling price/willingness-to-pay per feature; some features show R&D spend exceeding incremental revenue generated

framework: 1. Examine historical performance: review revenue and cost trends over time to confirm and quantify the profit decline
2. Analyze market dynamics and competitive positioning: assess each product segment's market share (absolute and relative) and competitive stability
3. Deep-dive into profitability drivers: evaluate COGS, SG&A, and critically R&D spending as the primary cost lever
4. Identify root cause in R&D: determine whether R&D is misallocated toward features customers do not value
5. Develop recommendation: cut or reallocate R&D spend and consider portfolio rationalization (exit weak segments, double down on leadership positions)

questions.prompt: After seeing Exhibit 1, what do you observe about Syzygy's financial trajectory and what would you want to investigate next?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note that revenues are roughly flat or growing while costs — especially one line item — are rising, compressing profits. Strong candidates will immediately ask to break down cost categories, particularly R&D, and request market-position data to understand whether the issue is revenue-side or cost-side.

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibits 2 and 3 together, identify which numbered bubble in Exhibit 3 corresponds to which product category in Exhibit 2, and explain your reasoning.
questions.guidance: The mapping logic: X-axis (AMS) in Exhibit 3 corresponds to the height of Syzygy's rectangles in Exhibit 2; Y-axis (RMS = Syzygy share / closest competitor share) corresponds to the ratio of Syzygy's rectangle height to competitors' for each product; bubble diameter reflects Syzygy's total revenues in the category (AMS x market size). Correct mapping: Product #1 = custom applications; Product #2 = supercomputers; Product #3 = telecom equipment; Product #4 = satellites; Product #5 = operating software. A strong candidate notes that Product #5 (operating software) has low AMS and low RMS — Syzygy is not the market leader there and faces structural disadvantage from network effects and the experience curve.

questions.prompt: What is the key insight from Exhibit 4 regarding Syzygy's R&D position relative to competitors?
questions.guidance: Syzygy is the only major competitor whose R&D spending falls below the normative band. Despite having slightly more R&D spending than Cray Research and Sonic Wave, Syzygy enjoys less perceived technical leadership from customers. This implies Syzygy's R&D is inefficient — the dollars spent are not translating into customer-perceived value or technical differentiation.

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 5 reveal about Syzygy's R&D spending on supercomputers, and what is the financial implication?
questions.guidance: Exhibit 5 shows that Syzygy is spending R&D dollars on features for which customers have low or no willingness-to-pay (i.e., the incremental selling price enabled by those features is less than the R&D cost to develop them). The correct analysis focuses on absolute R&D expense levels, not percentages. Strong candidates will note that trimming or redirecting this spend would directly improve profitability without sacrificing customer value.

math.setup: Compare R&D expense per feature to incremental customer willingness-to-pay (selling price increment) for that feature. If R&D cost > revenue uplift, that feature destroys value.
steps: Identify features where R&D spend exceeds incremental revenue/willingness-to-pay from Exhibit 5
Sum the excess R&D spend across those features to quantify the savings opportunity
Note that redirecting this spend toward high-WTP features could simultaneously cut costs and increase revenues
math.answer: The exact dollar figure depends on Exhibit 5 data; conceptually, eliminating value-destroying R&D features would close a meaningful portion of the profit gap on the supercomputers product line.

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond fixing R&D allocation, what other strategic actions should Syzygy consider to improve long-term profitability?

categories.name: Portfolio rationalization
ideas: Exit operating software (Product #5) where Syzygy has low absolute and relative market share and faces adverse network/scale economics
Double down on categories where Syzygy is market leader (high RMS) to exploit economies of scale and experience curve advantages against competitors

categories.name: R&D reallocation
ideas: Cut total R&D budget to bring spending within the normative band seen in Exhibit 4
Redirect R&D toward features with demonstrated customer willingness-to-pay above cost
Establish a feature-prioritization framework linking R&D investment to incremental revenue potential

categories.name: Revenue enhancement
ideas: Increase investment in products where Syzygy has strong market leadership to widen competitive moat
Explore premium pricing in segments where technical leadership is established
Grow market share in high-value categories (supercomputers, telecom equipment) where scale benefits accrue

categories.name: Cost discipline
ideas: Benchmark all cost lines (COGS, SG&A) against competitors even though they appear in-line today
Implement stage-gate process for R&D projects to kill low-ROI features early
Assess whether product line complexity across 5 categories creates shared-cost inefficiencies

recommendation: Syzygy should immediately reallocate or reduce R&D spending — either cut total R&D to eliminate investment in features customers are unwilling to pay for, or shift the same budget toward features with proven willingness-to-pay that exceeds R&D cost
Syzygy should exit the operating software business (Product #5) where low market share, network effects, and the experience curve all work against it, freeing resources for higher-return segments
Syzygy should concentrate investment and commercial focus on categories where it holds market leadership to deepen competitive advantages and harvest scale/experience-curve benefits
risks: Cutting R&D too aggressively could erode technical leadership perception in core products
Exiting operating software may create integration complications if it bundles with other Syzygy products
Reallocation requires accurate identification of which features drive customer WTP — misjudging this could misallocate the savings
next_steps: Conduct detailed customer research to map each R&D feature to incremental willingness-to-pay
Analyze operating software exit feasibility — revenue impact, customer contracts, integration dependencies
Develop a stage-gate R&D governance process to enforce ongoing ROI discipline
Model the profit improvement from eliminating value-destroying R&D features to set a target
